name: Aminyl
aliases: amido radical, amidogen, amino radical, azanyl, NH2(.)
summary: In chemistry, the amino radical, ·NH2, also known as the aminyl or azanyl, is the neutral form of the amide ion (NH−2). Aminyl radicals are highly reactive and consequently short-lived, like most radicals; however, they form an important part of nitrogen chemistry. In sufficiently high concentration, amino radicals dimerise to form hydrazine.g. the phenethylamines), the radical cannot be isolated in its free form.
